gaps.en: imperative: -ε to one person, -τε to several or politely
will you have something to eat?
how do you say this in Greek?

gaps.word: ο φίλος → τον φίλο → του φίλου

gaps.en: every noun has a gender and carries its article: ο δρόμος, η πόρτα, το κλειδί; plurals οι δρόμοι, οι πόρτες, τα κλειδιά
what time does the ferry go?
shall I make you a coffee?
to have a bath; to swim

gaps.word: κάνε μου / δώσε μου / φέρε μου
gaps.en: imperative + μου/μας turns an order into a request done for me/us: φέρε μου νερό

gaps.word: να φας / να προσέχεις / να περάσεις καλά
gaps.en: να + verb as a warm nudge or wish – the family register: 'do eat something', 'mind how you go'
every verb has two stems: imperfective for ongoing or repeated, perfective for a one-off – θα τρώω vs θα φάω
present perfect: έχω + one unchanging verb form
gerund: 'while doing' – φεύγοντας, τον είδα; for 'having done X, then Y' Greek just uses αφού or και

gaps.word: είκοσι ένα, τριάντα δύο, ενενήντα εννιά
gaps.en: 21–99: decade word + unit, kept as two separate words; only 1, 3 and 4 change for gender

gaps.word: πιο μεγάλος από / ο πιο μεγάλος
gaps.en: comparative and superlative: πιο + adjective + από; add the article for 'the most'
shall I take my shoes off?
send it to me on WhatsApp

gaps.word: Ποιος είναι ο κωδικός για το wi-fi;

gaps.en: mood, spirits, being up for it
in-law terms split by the relation, not by whose side: spouse's parents = πεθερικά, spouse's sibling = κουνιάδος/κουνιάδα, your sibling's or child's spouse = γαμπρός/νύφη
did you turn the gas off?
I need something for a fever
the question / relative / here-there grid: question word, its relative twin, and the two demonstratives
go (in order) to do: Πάω να φάω, Βγήκαμε να δούμε τη θέα
what will you let it go for?

gaps.word: πρώτη Μαΐου, δύο Μαΐου, δεκαπέντε Αυγούστου
gaps.en: dates: ordinal only for the 1st, plain numbers after, month in the genitive

gaps.word: η γυναίκα μου / ο άντρας μου
Όπου να 'ναι φεύγω / Ετοιμάζομαι να φύγω
gaps.en: about to: any minute now I'm off / I'm just about to leave
sit down and have something to eat
ring me when you get there

gaps.word: μπ = b · ντ = d · γκ/γγ = g · ου = u
gaps.en: reading Greek aloud: μπίρα is 'bira', ντομάτα 'domata', Αγγλία 'Anglía'; and ει, οι, η, υ, ι all say 'ee'

tooLate.en: present tense: κάνω = I do / I'm doing
here you are; go ahead; sorry?
yes? / here you are / sorry, what?
far too much; a great deal
the written accent marks the stressed syllable, and it is sometimes the only thing separating two words: πότε (when) vs ποτέ (never), γέρος (old man) vs γερός (strong)
hundreds: 200 διακόσια, 300 τριακόσια, 500 πεντακόσια; feminine διακόσιες, masculine διακόσιοι
